subject: Preemptible fanout policy & throughput assurances for Dedicated nodes
messages:
From: Sam Richards <sam.richards@lynxtelemetry.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lynxtelemetry.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 17:18:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated nodes question — preemptible fanout & latency guarantees

Hi Kimberly / Ben,

We're kicking off an internal evaluation for Dedicated capacity to support our realtime telemetry ingest and inference (Lynx Telemetry). Two quick things procurement and platform want to understand before we proceed to SOW:

1) How preemption behaves when capacity is tight — specifically, do you "fan out" preemptible work across tenants (we've heard the term "preemptible fanout") or do you evict per-tenant? How do you prevent noisy neighbors from pushing latency above our threshold?

2) What operational runway / failover exists if a reserved GPU is reclaimed (queueing behavior, KV/prefix cache preservation, and any short-term routing to hosted variants). We need concrete numbers (max queue delay, failover time window, and any throttling/backoff the runtime applies).

Procurement also attached a draft SOW for reference; security will send the questionnaire separately. Can you point us to any runbooks or example SLA clauses you’ve used for customers with 99.9x latency targets?

Thanks — happy to schedule a 30m sync if easier.

— Sam
Sam Richards
Head of Platform, Lynx Telemetry

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sam Richards <sam.richards@lynxtelemetry.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated nodes question — preemptible fanout & latency guarantees

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear note. This is exactly the sort of nuance we expect on Dedicated deals and we have a couple of patterns that map well to Lynx’s realtime constraints. TL;DR: we can offer a documented operational "latency shield" plus a short failover runway; below are concrete behaviors and a proposed clause to include in the SOW.

Behavioral summary (high level):
- Reservation model: reserved GPUs are single-tenant and not preempted for other customers; non-reserved (burst) capacity may be reclaimed under load.
- Preemptible fanout: when we reclaim burst capacity we do not aggressively evict tenant in-flight requests — instead we apply a fanout and queuing policy that attempts to preserve tail latency for active sessions (eviction deferral policy).
- Queueing limits: default queue hold is bounded per-request; we can set an agreed max queue delay and a per-tenant inflight-concurrency leash.
- Failover runway: automatic routing to gracefully degrade to a compatible hosted model variant with a typical handover window of 45–90s depending on model size and KV warming requirements.

Proposed SLA wording for SOW (draft language):
"Redwood will provide Dedicated reserved nodes with a 99.9% throughput availability target measured over 1-minute windows. During capacity reclamation events Redwood will apply an eviction deferral policy (latency shield) that aims to keep 95% of requests under a negotiated queueing delay threshold (default 150ms) for up to 60s of runway. If workload cannot be served on reserved nodes within the runway, requests will fail over to a hosted-compatible model; Redwood will use prefix/KV warming heuristics to minimize cold-start amplification."

I don't want to bury details in a single email — Ben, can you drop the technical appendix here (observability metrics and crediting formula) and we’ll propose a short sync for tomorrow?

— Kimberly

On Tue, Jul 20, 2027 at 09:04 Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> I don't want to bury details in a single email — Ben, can you drop the technical appendix here

Hi Sam — adding the appendix below. Quick note: a lot of the runtime behavior is tunable per-account; we can harden conservative defaults in the SOW.

Technical appendix (summary):
- Measurement windows: throughput availability = successful tokens emitted / expected tokens per 1-minute window.
- Latency shielding controls:
  * Inflight-concurrency leash: configurable per-deployment (default 20 concurrent requests).
  * Max queue delay (95th): default 150ms, can be tightened to 75–100ms for premium queues.
  * Eviction deferral: for up to N seconds (configurable; default 60s) we avoid evicting warm KV cache entries and attempt to schedule on adjacent reserved nodes before fallback.
- Failover behavior:
  * Runway: 45–90s graceful reroute to hosted-compatible variant.
  * Cold-start mitigation: prefix/KV warming and short-term cache replication for small models (<6B) reduces regression.
- Crediting and remediation:
  * If Redwood breaches the negotiated availability target, credits apply on a per-minute basis using the formula in Appendix A of the SOW.
  * Emergency headroom: for qualifying annual commitments we can offer a transient headroom pool to minimize customer-visible failover.

Attachments & links: the preemptive-fanout runbook above is internal but we can share a redacted link for procurement review: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-preemptive-fanout-runbook

Actions:
- Kimberly: propose 30m sync to agree the queueing threshold and runway (I can bring an infra engineer).
- Sam: suggest target SLO (e.g., 99.9 vs 99.95) and whether procurement needs a guaranteed hard cap on queue delay.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — really helpful. A couple of follow-ups from platform/procurement after reviewing the appendix:

- Platform asks if we can tighten the 95th queue delay to 100ms for the ingest path (we can accept a slightly higher failover rate if necessary).
- Procurement would like a hard service-level number for runway (we prefer a guaranteed 60s runway window and a written crediting formula we can include in the contract).
- Security mentioned a few questions about cache replication (do you encrypt KV replication in transit? how are keys rotated?). We'll attach the questionnaire soon.

We want to avoid live site surprises during a large spike (think: fleet upgrade + marketing event). Also — is there a temporary carveout option for predictable high-traffic days (an add-on headroom pool)? If so, what's lead time and pricing model?

If you can update the draft SOW with the tighter queueing number and the 60s runway guarantee, procurement can take it to legal. We can do a 30m call tomorrow morning (09:00 ET) if that works for your team.

— Sam
